newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Wild Taiwan stocks close lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Wild Taiwan stocks close lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Profit-taking sapped Taiwan share prices on Friday in a wild session that saw market turnover hit a three-year high on the way to a lower close, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 36.77 points or 0.49 percent lower at 7,499.51 after fluctuating in a wide range with a peak of 7,606.00 and a trough of 7,485.03.
Turnover was a frantic T$144 billion, surpassing the T$141.62 billion on January 10, 1994, and marking the highest total since T$152.13 billion on January 7, 1994.
The market had opened higher on momentum from eight consecutive sessions of gains.
"The market is becoming immune to all these rumours on Deng, because none of the rumours ever proves to be real," said George Hou, fund manager for Jardine Fleming.
The unsubstantiated rumours had helped send Hong Kong's stock index tumbling some 1.15 percent in early trade.

Taiwan construction shares defied day's downturn, climbing 1.90 percent as some investors continued to buy shares as an inflation hedge after newspapers recently reported that charges for water and electricity may rise in 1997, brokers said.
Brokers expected the index to trade in a 7,450-7,550 range on Saturday before resuming its rise next week.
